cards.text: Jesus is on the move again, heading on from there. Two blind men are following Him, and they're shouting at Him the whole way. Friend, they can't SEE Him, and they're still keeping up. Me? I lose track of a cookie tray I'm HOLDING.

cards.question: As the two blind men follow Jesus, what are they crying out for?

cards.text: 'Have mercy on us, Son of David!' Not 'hey, Teacher.' Not 'excuse me, sir.' They call Him by a name that points all the way back to David, Israel's king.

cards.question: Jesus goes inside a house. The two blind men give up and stay outside.

cards.text: Nope. They come right in to Him. Blind, inside a house, and they STILL find Him, while I can't find a rolling pin in my own bakery with the lights ON. Before Jesus does anything, He asks them one question.

cards.question: Before He heals the two blind men, what does Jesus ask them?

answers.text: Do you believe that I am able to do this
How long have you both been blind
Who told you where to find Me

cards.text: No hemming, no hawing. 'Yes, Lord,' they answer, and Jesus touches their eyes.

cards.question: As He touches their eyes, Jesus tells the two men it will be done to them according to their ___.

cards.text: Their eyes are OPENED! And the very next thing Jesus does is get stern with them.

cards.question: What does Jesus sternly warn the two men He just healed?

answers.text: See that no one finds out about this
Go and show yourselves to the priest
Follow Me wherever I go from here

cards.question: The two healed men do what Jesus says and keep the news to themselves.

cards.text: Keep it quiet? They go out and spread the news about Him through the WHOLE land. Friend, I can't keep quiet about a batch that came out perfectly round, and these men just got their EYES back.
As they're leaving, people bring another man to Jesus. This one has a demon, and he can't speak.

cards.question: When the demon is driven out, the man who couldn't speak begins to talk.
When the man starts talking, the crowds watching are ___.

cards.text: The crowds say, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!” The man who couldn't say a word is talking, and now the WHOLE crowd is talking.
But not everybody's cheering. The Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, see the same thing and come up with an explanation of their own.

cards.question: What do the Pharisees say about how Jesus drives out demons?

answers.text: It is by the prince of demons
It is by the power of Elijah
It is by magic learned in Egypt

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Jesus is on the move again, heading on from there." / "Two blind men are following Him..." / "Friend, they can't SEE Him, and they're still keeping up." / "Me? I lose track of a cookie tray I'm HOLDING." The limit for an opening card is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a thought ("As Jesus went on from there", 9:27). The card repeats "heading on from there" but never says where "there" is or what just happened before this scene, so it gives no context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "they're shouting at Him the whole way" stretches the text. Matthew 9:27 says only that they "followed Him, crying out." It does not say they kept crying out for the whole journey.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: the quote, "Not 'hey, Teacher.'", "Not 'excuse me, sir.'" and "They call Him by a name...". A story card that is not the opening card can have only one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Keep it quiet?" / "They go out and spread the news..." / "Friend, I can't keep quiet about a batch...". A story card can have only one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Cards 1 and 5 use the same joke: the blind men keep track of Jesus, but Papa Dorin can't keep track of things (a cookie tray, a rolling pin). Both jokes are built on the men's blindness. The jokes admire the men and make Papa Dorin the joke. Still, the hard rules list groups that are never joked about, and disability is not on that list. The docs also don't say whether he can reuse the same joke setup within one stop.
findings.question: Is humor that plays on a Bible character's disability (here, the men's blindness) allowed if it admires them and makes Papa Dorin the joke? Should the docs also say whether Papa Dorin can reuse the same joke setup twice in one stop?
